problem.text: The isosceles right triangle $ABC$ has right angle at $C$ and area $12.5$. The rays trisecting $\angle ACB$ intersect $AB$ at $D$ and $E$. What is the area of $\triangle CDE$?

steps.title: Where to start: a 45-45-90 triangle cut into 30 degree angles
steps.body: The problem gives two special facts: the triangle is an isosceles right triangle (angles $45^\circ$, $45^\circ$, $90^\circ$), and the $90^\circ$ angle at $C$ is trisected into three $30^\circ$ angles. Angles of $30^\circ$ and $45^\circ$ together are the clue that we can split pieces into $30$-$60$-$90$ and $45$-$45$-$90$ triangles. First find the legs from the area.

your_turn.prompt: If both legs have length $\ell$ and the area is $12.5$, what is $\ell$?

steps.title: Area of $CDE$ by subtraction
steps.body: Say $D$ is the point nearer $A$. Triangle $CDE$ is what is left of $ABC$ after removing triangles $ACD$ and $BCE$. Reflecting the picture across the bisector of $\angle C$ swaps $A$ with $B$ and swaps the two trisecting rays, so $[ACD] = [BCE]$ (square brackets mean area). So $[CDE] = 12.5 - 2[ACD]$.

your_turn.prompt: What are the three angles of triangle $ACD$?

steps.title: Drop a perpendicular from $D$
steps.body: A $30$-$45$-$105$ triangle splits into two special triangles. Drop a perpendicular from $D$ to $AC$, meeting it at $Y$. Triangle $AYD$ has a $45^\circ$ angle at $A$ and a right angle at $Y$, so it is isosceles: call $AY = YD = x$. Triangle $DYC$ has a right angle at $Y$ and a $30^\circ$ angle at $C$.

your_turn.prompt: In triangle $DYC$, write $YC$ in terms of $x$.
your_turn.answer: $YD = x$ is opposite the $30^\circ$ angle, so it is the short leg, and the long leg is $YC = x\sqrt{3}$.

steps.title: Solve for the height $x$
steps.body:
The two pieces make up side $AC$:
$$AY + YC = x + x\sqrt{3} = 5.$$

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body:
In triangle $ACD$, take $AC = 5$ as the base; $YD = x$ is the height. So $[ACD] = \frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot\frac{5\sqrt{3}-5}{2} = \frac{25\sqrt{3}-25}{4}$, and
$$[CDE] = \frac{25}{2} - 2\cdot\frac{25\sqrt{3}-25}{4} = \frac{25 - 25\sqrt{3} + 25}{2} = \frac{50-25\sqrt{3}}{2}.$$ The answer is **(D)**.
